sentences.text: This pterosaur possessed a massive skull reaching sixty-one centimeters in length.
Its total wingspan extended to five meters, supporting a body mass of twenty kilograms.
A symmetrical crest sat atop its snout, measuring twelve centimeters long with a maximum height of seventeen millimeters.
The fourth tooth in the upper jaw measured eighty-one millimeters, representing the largest known tooth length for any pterosaur.
Wang Xiaolin and Zhou Zhonghe named the genus in 2003.
The species Liaoningopterus gui serves as the type species for the group.
Researchers suggest it was a piscivore, feeding on fish due to its long, pointed snout.
Wang classified the animal within the Anhangueridae family, primarily because of its crests.
A 2006 cladistic analysis by Lü Junchang indicated it was a basal member of that family.
Later, a 2008 study by Ji Qiang placed it in a trichotomy with Anhanguera and Tropeognathus.
Under David Unwin's alternative terminology, it is considered a member of the Ornithocheiridae.
The parent group for this taxon is Ornithocheiroidea.
It lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
